transcript:
User: Hi. Saw your ad. Honestly I doubt this is for us but go ahead.
Agent: Got it — you saw our ad, and you’re not sure it’s a fit. What made you click in the first place?
User: Curiosity mostly. We already have an answering service, so I'm skeptical about needing something else.
Agent: Makes sense—if you’ve already got an answering service, you shouldn’t add anything unless it’s clearly better. What’s been happening that still feels not quite handled with your current setup?
User: I wouldn't say there's an issue. We just want to explore options, but cost's a big factor too.
Agent: Yeah, totally fair—if cost’s a big factor, it only makes sense to look if you’re missing anything today. When a call comes in and your answering service doesn’t pick up (or the caller hangs up), what usually happens next?
User: We usually follow up, but we miss about 10 calls a week. Not ideal, obviously.
Agent: Got it—about 10 a week is meaningful, especially if you’re having to chase them after. What kind of business are you in?
User: We're a dental practice in Phoenix, Arizona. Most missed calls could convert to bookings with proper handling.
Agent: Got it — dental in Phoenix, and those missed calls are likely appointments if they’re handled right. When those 10 calls a week are missed, do they usually call back later, or do you feel like many just book somewhere else?
User: Many don't call back. We estimate 40% would book if we caught them. What's this going to cost?
Agent: Makes sense—if many don’t call back, price really matters because it’s either paying for coverage or losing those bookings. Before we talk cost, mind if I do a quick 30‑second calculation using your numbers so we know what “worth it” even means?
User: Sure, but I need a number soon or I'm done. What’s a ballpark for similar services?
Agent: I hear you — ballpark, most dental offices see something in the low hundreds to a couple thousand per month depending on call volume and what you want it to handle, plus sometimes a one-time setup. 

So I don’t waste your time, what’s your average value for a booked appointment — are we talking $200, $300, $500?
User: $700 on average. But how do I know this isn't some sketchy startup that disappears with our patient data?
Agent: Got it — $700 helps. And yeah, protecting patient data is non‑negotiable.

Before I answer, are you mainly worried about HIPAA/security controls, or about company stability and support if something breaks?
User: Company stability and support are my main concerns. I need assurance you're not going to vanish on us.
Agent: Totally fair — if something touches your phones, you need to know there’s real support behind it. What would “stable enough” look like for you: a month‑to‑month with no long commitment, or specific things like references/case studies and an SLA-style support response time?
User: I’d need references, case studies, and strong support response times before considering anything further.
Agent: Makes sense — that’s exactly how a dental office should vet something like this. If we could show you dental references/case studies and clear support response times, would you be open to running the quick math on what those missed calls are costing you first?
User: Sure, but I tried one of these AI things last year, it was garbage and wasted three months.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — three months wasted would make anyone skeptical. What specifically made it “garbage” last time: it couldn’t book properly, it sounded unnatural, or it didn’t hand off to your team the right way?
User: It couldn't book properly and sounded really unnatural. Customers weren't impressed, and it hurt our reputation.
Agent: Ugh, yeah — if it sounded robotic and couldn’t actually book, that’s worse than missing the call. 

So I can keep this grounded in your numbers: those ~10 missed calls a week, and you said about 40% would book if caught — what scheduling system are you on (Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Open Dental, something else)?
User: We're using Dentrix. But how do I know your system won’t have the same issues as the last one?
Agent: Got it — Dentrix. And that’s the right question after a bad experience: what would you need to see or hear in a demo to feel confident it can actually book naturally without risking your reputation?
User: I need to see smooth, natural booking demos and patient feedback to trust it won't harm our reputation.
Agent: That makes total sense — you’d want to hear it handle a real booking naturally and see what actual patients said afterward. 

Quick math so we anchor this: with ~10 missed calls a week and ~40% booking rate, what’s your average value per booked patient (or first visit) — is it the $700 you mentioned?
User: Yes, our average value per booked patient is $700. So, tell me about tomorrow afternoon, what does that entail?
Agent: Got it — with your numbers, that’s roughly **$12,100/month** in missed bookings. Tomorrow afternoon would be a 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay where he shows natural booking demos, how it works with Dentrix, and the dental references/support expectations—what’s better for you, later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow afternoon works. Call +16025550017 to confirm. Looking forward to seeing how this could help us.
Agent: Perfect — and we’ll use the number you’re calling from ending **0017**. What’s your first name?
User: It's Brenda. Looking forward to seeing what you have to offer. Thanks for addressing all my concerns!
Agent: Got it, Brenda — appreciate you being open about the last experience. What’s your last name?
User: It's Kowalski. Thanks for understanding my concerns. Looking forward to the call and seeing how this can help us.
Agent: Got it, Brenda Kowalski. What’s the name of your dental practice?
User: Desert Bloom Dental in Phoenix. We're eager to learn how your service can improve our patient bookings.
Agent: Got it — Desert Bloom Dental. And just to confirm, is the number you’re calling from (+1 602‑555‑0017) the best number to reach you for the appointment details?
User: Actually, the best number is +16025550017. Please use that one for the appointment details.
Agent: Got it — we’ll use **+1 602‑555‑0017**. For **tomorrow afternoon (Mountain time)**, I can get you in at **3:00 PM** or **3:45 PM**—which works?
User: Actually, use +16025550017. And it's Arizona time, not Mountain. Let's go with 3:45 PM tomorrow.
Agent: Got it — **3:45 PM tomorrow**, and we’ll use **+1 602‑555‑0017**. So that’s **Friday, Aug 28 at 3:45 PM Arizona time**, correct?
User: No, correct number is +16025550017. It's Thursday, not Friday. 3:45 PM Arizona time works. Confirm that, please.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: All set, Brenda — you’re booked for **tomorrow at 3:45 PM Arizona time**, and we’ll use **+1 602‑555‑0017**; you’ll get an SMS confirmation with the details and an add-to-calendar link. Is there anything else I can help you with?
User: Sure, I'll wait. Just to confirm, 3:45 PM Arizona time tomorrow at +16025550017.
Agent: Exactly — tomorrow at 3:45 PM Arizona time, and we’ll call you at +1 602‑555‑0017; the SMS confirmation is on the way. Really glad you called, Brenda — Jay’s looking forward to it. Have a great rest of your day. Bye!
